Compare a first-time viewer's understanding of a promo clip with the truth.
TRUTH (from the show bible, for episodes E8): Premise: [mock] Mara is accused of theft at her sister's betrothal feast until a hooded harbourmaster speaks for her.
Mayor Brisk (a figure in period dress): [mock] speaks 53 lines between E1 and E14
Selene (a figure in period dress): [mock] speaks 46 lines between E1 and E14
Widow Halloran (a figure in period dress): [mock] speaks 45 lines between E1 and E14
Tobin The Ferryman (a man in period dress): [mock] speaks 40 lines between E1 and E14
Corin (a figure in period dress): [mock] speaks 37 lines between E1 and E14
Arc [mock] Part 3: Corin's past returns on a ship flying a black pennant.
E8: Mara discovers her father's logbook hidden in the lamp room.
CLIP: [On screen: Wide shot of the storm-lashed harbour, lanterns swinging on the quay.]
a man in period dress: "Your father paid me to watch over you."
[On screen: Close-up on the figure in period dress's jaw tightening.]
[On screen: Over-the-shoulder shot from the man in period dress toward the figure in period dress.]
a figure in period dress: "The council has already decided her fate."
[On screen: Wide shot of the storm-lashed harbour, lanterns swinging on the quay.]
[Action: the the figure in period dress tears the lace veil and lets it fall.]
a figure in period dress: "Every wedding needs a widow. Why not two?"
[On screen: Tight shot on a silver ring glinting in candlelight.]
a figure in period dress: "Nobody leaves this hall until I say so."
[On screen: High wide shot of the crowded hall turning toward the door.]
a figure in period dress: "Say her name again and you will regret it."
[Sound: Glass shatters on stone.]
[On screen: Over-the-shoulder shot from the figure in period dress toward the figure in period dress.]
a figure in period dress (off-screen): "Order! I will have order in my hall!"
[On screen: Over-the-shoulder shot from the the figure in period dress toward the widow.]
[Action: the widow tears the lace veil and lets it fall.]
a figure in period dress: "He is lying. Everyone knows he is lying!"
